title: Guru Nanak’s revelation at Sultanpur and the Sikh tradition
summary: In Sikh tradition, Guru Nanak, born in 1469 at Talwandi in Punjab, had a profound religious experience at about the age of thirty, dated to 1499, while living at Sultanpur Lodi, where he had worked in the governor’s stores. He later founded the settlement of Kartarpur on the Ravi, where a community gathered around him.

uncertainty.note: The year 1499 is a traditional date, given by one source as the year Nanak was thirty. Another says only "around 30 years old".

as_recorded.value: Guru Nanak was thirty years old at this time in 1499
When he was around 30 years old, he had a profound religious experience

where.modern_name: Sultanpur Lodhi, Kapurthala district, Punjab, India
where.historical_name: Sultanpur (Sultanpur Lodi), Punjab, under the Muslim governor Daulat Khan Lodi

importance.justification: The traditional starting point of the Sikh community, centred on Guru Nanak and his later settlement at Kartarpur.

reviewer_note: Least sure: 1499 is a traditional date reckoned from the 1469 birth and "age thirty"; Patheos says "around 30". The Sultanpur setting is also from tradition (a river experience). Kartarpur (founded later) is not pinned here. No Sikh record exists yet in the atlas to link.
